entities.name: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
entities.label: Idea
entities.summary:
The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), formally established on June 15, 2001, in Shanghai, China, represents a pivotal Eurasian political, economic, and security alliance aimed at fostering regional stability and cooperation among its member states. Emerging from the "Shanghai Five" mechanism, which began in 1996 to demilitarize borders following the collapse of the Soviet Union, the SCO quickly evolved into a significant counterweight to Western influence, particularly in Central Asia. Its membership, initially comprising China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan, has since expanded to include India, Pakistan, and Iran, making it the world's largest regional organization by geographic scope and population, encompassing over 40% of the global populace and 20% of global GDP.

The SCO's foundational charter, signed in 2002 and entering into force in 2003, outlines its core objectives: strengthening mutual trust and good-neighborliness, promoting effective cooperation in politics, trade, economy, science and technology, culture, education, energy, transportation, tourism, and environmental protection. Key initiatives include regular summits of Heads of State, foreign ministers, and security council secretaries, alongside the establishment of the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) in Tashkent in 2004 to combat terrorism, separatism, and extremism. The SCO has also facilitated joint military exercises, such as the "Peace Mission" series, demonstrating its commitment to collective security and coordinated responses to regional threats.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation has profoundly reshaped Eurasian geopolitics by creating a powerful non-Western security and economic bloc, integrating over 40% of the world's population and challenging traditional unipolar global structures. Its expansion to include major powers like India, Pakistan, and Iran underscores its growing influence as a key player in a multipolar world.
